footer.promise: {{server}} runs on your own machine. Orchester Cloud only confirms who signs in; your projects never pass through it.

error.unavailable: The server is not answering right now. Try again in a minute.
error.refused: The server did not accept this. Check the fields and try again.
error.forbidden: You are not allowed to do this here.
error.gone: That is no longer there. Reload the page.
error.formExpired: This form has expired. Reload the page and try again.
error.tooManyTries: Too many tries from your network. Try again in {{minutes}} min, at {{time}}.
error.emailInvalid: Enter a full email address, like name@example.com.
error.nameLong: Use at most {{max}} characters; this one has {{count}}.
error.codeShape: A code has 8 characters, like ABCD-EFGH.

failure.title: The server is not answering
failure.description: This page could not be loaded. Try again in a minute.
failure.missingDescription: Check the address, or start from the admin's first page.

projects.title: Projects
projects.description: Each project has its own address on this server. People link their checkout to that address in Orchester; everyone clones the code themselves, the server never touches it.
projects.descriptionPhone: Each project has its own address on this server. People link their checkout to it in Orchester.
projects.descriptionOwner: You own these projects, so you see them with their Members and Invites. People, Devices and Settings are for admins.
projects.noteAdmin: Admins see every project on {{server}}. A project owner who isn't an admin sees only the projects they own.
projects.emptyText: Create one by name and slug; it gets its own address on this server.
projects.emptyOwnerText: You own no project on {{server}} now. An admin creates projects.
projects.waitingTitle: A computer is waiting for approval
projects.waitingText: Orchester on {{device}} wants to join as {{name}}. Join approval is on, so it waits for one of their computers or an admin.
projects.waitingTextMany: Join approval is on, so they wait for one of their person's computers or an admin.
projects.notePhone: Tasks and runs are in Orchester on your computer; these pages run the server.

project.missingText: This project does not exist on {{server}}, or you don't manage it.

members.description: Members see {{project}}'s tasks and its shared configuration in Orchester. Owners manage members and invites; a new role applies at once on every member's computer.
members.removeText: They lose access to {{project}} at once. Their computers keep a local copy of the tasks they had; their account on {{server}} stays.
members.leaveText: You lose access to {{project}} at once. Your computers keep a local copy of its tasks; your account on {{server}} stays.
members.lastOwnerText: You're its only owner, so you can't leave or become a member. Make someone else an owner first.
members.lastOwnerOther: {{name}} is its only owner, so they can't be removed or become a member. Make someone else an owner first.
members.removedText: Their computers keep a local copy of its tasks; their account on {{server}} stays.
members.note: Removing someone ends their access to {{project}} at once; their computers keep the tasks they had, as a local copy. Their account on {{server}} stays, with its other projects.

invites.emailText: Orchester Cloud delivers it: in Orchester if they have an account, and by email either way. Someone new is asked to create an account first. It expires in 7 days.
invites.codeText: For a computer without the internet. They enter {{project}}'s address and the 8-character code in Orchester, compare the check code, and choose a username. The code works once, for 72 hours, and is shown only once.
invites.codeWarning: Give these three to the person yourself. This is the only time the code is shown: Orchester keeps only a fingerprint of it. Lost it? Revoke it and make a new one.
invites.noCheckCode: None: the server is behind a proxy with its own certificate
invites.sentText: Orchester Cloud delivers it in Orchester and by email. It's open until {{when}}.
invites.browserText: The invite to {{email}} is made and signed by the server. Send it from this browser; it reaches them in Orchester and by email as usual.
invites.refusedTitle: Orchester Cloud did not take the invite
invites.refusedText: The invite to {{email}} is made on {{server}}, but the cloud refused it. Revoke it, check the link in Settings, or invite with a code.
invites.noCloudText: This admin has no address for Orchester Cloud (ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL), so it can't send them. Invite with a code instead.
invites.unlinkedText: {{server}} isn't linked to Orchester Cloud. Link it in Settings, or invite with a code.
invites.limitText: That's the limit per person. Try again at {{time}}, or invite with a code.
invites.tooManyCodes: There are too many open codes on {{server}}. Revoke some, or let them expire.
invites.mfaText: Turn on two-factor authentication in your Orchester Cloud account to send invites. Then sign out here and sign in again with Orchester Cloud.
invites.mfaCodeText: Making invites, codes too, needs two-factor authentication: sign in to this admin through Orchester Cloud with it, or with a pairing code made in Orchester on a computer that joined with it.
invites.listText: An invite ends when it's accepted, expires or is revoked. Revoking stops it at once, in Orchester Cloud too.
invites.byCode: By code · {{when}} · the code isn't shown again
invites.endedNote: By email · sent by {{name}}, {{when}} · the address is forgotten once an invite ends
invites.revokeText: It stops working at once, in Orchester Cloud too. You can invite them again later.
invites.revokeTextCode: It stops working at once. You can make a new one later.
invites.revokedCloudLater: It no longer works on {{server}}. Orchester Cloud could not be told now, so the invitation email may still arrive; accepting it fails.
invites.emptyText: Invites to {{project}} show here while they are open, and for 30 days after they end.

projectSettings.name: Name
projectSettings.nameHint: Shown in Orchester and on invites. You can change it any time.
projectSettings.addressHint: Fixed. The address is how every member's Orchester knows this project, so its slug, {{slug}}, never changes.
projectSettings.hintHelp: The origin remote this project's code usually comes from. When someone links a checkout with a different origin, Orchester warns them and lets them go on. The server never touches the code. Empty clears it.
projectSettings.ownersHint: Owners manage members and invites. Change roles in Members.

newProject.title: New project
newProject.description: Create a project on {{server}}. You become its owner; invite people once it exists.
newProject.name: Name
newProject.nameHint: Shown in Orchester and on invites.
newProject.slugHint: Small letters, digits and hyphens. The slug becomes the project's address and can't change once the project is created; the name can.
newProject.hintHelp: Orchester warns whoever links a checkout with a different origin.
newProject.note: Already working on it in Orchester, with local tasks? Create the project here, then link your local project to its address in Orchester (Project settings › Sharing). Its tasks are uploaded with their numbers.
newProject.slugTaken: Another project on {{server}} has this address. Choose another slug.
newProject.slugReserved: {{slug}} is kept for the server itself. Choose another slug.
newProject.slugShape: Use small letters, digits and hyphens.
newProject.slugShapeLike: Use small letters, digits and hyphens, like {{slug}}.
newProject.createdText: Its address is {{address}}. Invite people, then link your local project to that address in Orchester.

people.title: People
people.description: Everyone with an account on {{server}}. Being here gives nothing by itself: people work only in the projects they're members of.
people.inviteText: For someone who needs an account here but no project yet, or a new admin. To add someone to a project, invite them from that project.
people.codeWarning: Give it to {{name}} yourself. In Orchester on their computer: Settings › Orchester › Connect a server, the address, the check code, then this code. It's shown only once.
people.disableText: Every computer of theirs is signed out of {{server}} at once and they can't join again until you enable it. Their tasks and history stay.
people.makeAdminText: They can then see and change every project, person, device and setting here.
people.unlinkText: Their Orchester Cloud account then signs in to nothing on {{server}}, and their computers stay joined. They link it again from one of their computers, or an account code links the account to the cloud account they enter it with.
people.lastAdminText: You're its only admin, so your account can't be disabled or lose admin. Make someone else an admin first.
people.sentTitleAdmin: Invite sent to {{email}}, as an admin
people.sentText: They get an account on {{server}} with no project. It's open until {{when}}; revoke it from the list below the form.
people.note: An account code gives a computer to someone who lost all of theirs: it works once, for 24 hours, and links the account to the Orchester Cloud account it's entered with. Admins get their next computer from their own computers or the server's console. Disabling signs out every computer of that account at once; their tasks and history stay.
people.adminsOnlyText: Admins of {{server}} manage its accounts. You see the projects you own.

devices.title: Devices
devices.description: Computers joined to {{server}}, one entry per computer and person. Revoking signs a computer out of {{server}} at once; changes waiting on it stay there until it joins again.
devices.waitingText: Join approval is on, so a new computer joining through Orchester Cloud waits. The person's own computers can approve it too; ask them if you don't expect it.
devices.refuseText: It doesn't join, and its Orchester says it was refused. If {{name}} didn't start this, someone else may be signed in to their Orchester account: tell them.
devices.approvedText: It joined as {{name}} and moves to Joined. Their other computers say a new one joined.
devices.refusedText: It doesn't join, and its Orchester says it was refused.
devices.unused: Unused for {{days}} days · expires in {{left}} days
devices.revokeText: It's signed out of {{server}} at once. Changes waiting on it stay there; it joins again through an invite or Orchester Cloud.
devices.revokedText: It joins again through an invite or Orchester Cloud.
devices.note: A computer unused for 90 days is signed out by itself. Revoked or expired, it joins again through an invite or Orchester Cloud.
devices.emptyText: Computers that join {{server}} with Orchester show here.
devices.noMatchText: Search by a person's name or username, or by the computer's name.
devices.adminsOnlyText: Admins of {{server}} see every joined computer. You see the projects you own.
devices.browsersText: Browsers where someone is signed in to the admin of {{server}}. A sign-in ends by itself 12 hours after it began; revoke one to end it now.
devices.browserRevokeTitle: Sign {{name}} out of the admin in that browser?
devices.browserRevokeText: That browser is signed out of the admin at once. Their computers stay joined.
devices.browserRevokedTitle: {{name}}'s browser is signed out of the admin
devices.browserRevokedText: Signing in again takes Orchester Cloud or a code.

settings.title: Settings
settings.description: How {{server}} trusts the people and computers that join it.
settings.joinOnHint: When someone who already has an account here joins from a new computer through Orchester Cloud, that computer waits until one of their joined computers or an admin approves it. Off by default. Invite codes and pairing codes are not affected.
settings.joinOffHint: New computers joining through Orchester Cloud join at once. Their other computers still say a new one joined.
settings.joinAlways: Their other computers always say when a new one joined, whichever way this is set.
settings.cloudText: The cloud vouches for who people are when they join with their Orchester account. It never sees projects.
settings.notLinkedText: Link it to invite people by email and let them join and sign in here with their Orchester account. Your browser carries the link to Orchester Cloud, where you sign in; {{server}} itself needs no internet.
settings.noCloudText: This admin has no address for Orchester Cloud (ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL), so it can't link from here.
settings.acceptingHint: Turn off to stop every join through Orchester Cloud at once. Computers already joined keep working, and invite codes still work.
settings.offTitle: Nobody joins through Orchester Cloud now
settings.offText: Joined computers keep working. New people join with invite codes; admins sign in here with a code.
settings.keyHint: The fingerprint of Orchester Cloud's root key, pinned when you linked. Its key list was last refreshed {{refreshed}}, and is good until {{until}}.
settings.keyHintNoList: The fingerprint of Orchester Cloud's root key, pinned when you linked. The server has no key list from the cloud yet.
settings.pinHint: Only after Orchester announces a new root key, or if you were told the old one leaked. Until it's pinned, cloud joins wait.
settings.pinEmpty: Paste the new root key Orchester announced.
settings.unlinkText: Joins through the cloud stop and open invites by email end. Joined computers keep working; codes still work. Orchester Cloud is told when the server can reach it.
settings.staleTitle: Orchester Cloud's keys here are out of date
settings.staleText: {{server}} hasn't reached Orchester Cloud for a while, so cloud joins stop until it does, or until a joining computer brings newer keys. Joined computers and codes keep working.
settings.staleLine: Key list last refreshed {{refreshed}}; it expired {{expired}}.
settings.checkHint: The same code the server prints to its console. A computer connecting by address compares it once; one that accepts an invite gets it from the invite; a browser opening these pages compares the certificate's SHA-256 fingerprint.
settings.certPem: From the certificate files in the server's configuration
settings.certHintSelf: To replace it, run orchester-server tls regenerate on the server. Every computer then stops until its person checks the new code.
settings.certHintPem: Replace the files and restart the server to change it. Every computer then stops until its person checks the new code.
settings.noCert: Plain HTTP behind a proxy: browsers and computers see the proxy's certificate, so there is no check code here.
settings.unlinked: {{server}} is no longer linked to Orchester Cloud.
settings.adminsOnly: Settings is for the admins of {{server}}.

signin.title: Sign in to {{server}}'s admin
signin.description: For admins and project owners. Work on tasks stays in Orchester.
signin.cloudHint: Your browser goes to {{host}} to confirm it's you, then comes back here. {{server}} itself needs no internet.
signin.codeHint: When this browser can't reach Orchester Cloud.
signin.cloudOffTitle: Sign-ins through Orchester Cloud are off
signin.cloudOffText: An admin turned them off on this server. Sign in with a code instead.
signin.unlinkedText: Admins sign in here with a code until it is linked.
signin.noCloudTitle: This admin has no address for Orchester Cloud
signin.noCloudText: Sign in with a code. Whoever runs the server sets ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL to use Orchester Cloud.
signin.approvalRequiredText: Signing in through Orchester Cloud needs one of your computers: in Orchester, Settings › Orchester › {{server}} › Sign in to the admin, then sign in here with that code.
signin.notInvitedText: That Orchester account has no account here. An admin can invite you.
signin.invalidIdentityTitle: Orchester Cloud's answer didn't check out
signin.invalidIdentityText: {{server}} could not check who Orchester Cloud vouched for. Start again.
signin.keySetStaleText: Its copy of Orchester Cloud's keys is too old to check the sign-in. Sign in with a code.
signin.cloudOffNow: They were turned off on this server while you signed in. Sign in with a code.
signin.tooManyText: Your network tried too often. Try again in a few minutes.
signin.tripLostText: It took too long, or came back to another browser. Start again.
signin.expiredText: Reload the page and start again.
signin.failedText: The server isn't answering. Try again in a minute.

code.title: Sign in with a code
code.description: Use a pairing code from Orchester on a computer joined to {{server}} as you (Settings › Orchester › {{server}} › Sign in to the admin), or an account code printed on the server (orchester-server account-code <username>).
code.hint: 8 characters, shown as ABCD-EFGH. Works once: a pairing code for 10 minutes, an account code for 24 hours.
code.wrong: That code isn't right, or it was used or has expired. A pairing code lasts 10 minutes, an account code 24 hours; make a new one in Orchester.
code.tooManyTitle: Too many wrong codes from this address
code.question: This browser reaches the internet?

nothing.title: Nothing to manage here
nothing.text: You're signed in as {{name}} ({{email}}). You don't administer {{server}} or own any of its projects, so these pages have nothing for you. Your work on its projects is in Orchester.
nothing.textNoName: You don't administer {{server}} or own any of its projects, so these pages have nothing for you. Your work on its projects is in Orchester.

https.title: This page needs HTTPS
https.text: The admin keeps you signed in with a cookie that only travels over HTTPS, so it doesn't work at {{origin}}.
https.open: Open {{secure}}, or, on the server itself, {{local}}.

address.title: Open this in Orchester
address.text: {{address}} is a project's address. In Orchester: Project settings › Sharing › Link to a project, or accept your invite. This page shows nothing about the project.

setup.title: Set up this Orchester server
setup.description: Nobody administers this server yet. Enter the setup code it printed to its console when it started; whoever enters it becomes its first admin.
setup.hint: Valid for 24 hours. The server prints a new one at each start until it has an admin.
setup.wrong: That isn't the setup code, or it has expired. The console shows the current one; restarting the server prints a new one.
setup.tooManyTitle: Too many wrong codes from this address
setup.alreadyText: This server has an admin, so it takes no setup code any more. Sign in instead; an admin can add you.
setup.accountText: You become the server's first admin. Teammates see your name next to your work.
setup.usernameShape: Use small letters, digits and hyphens.
setup.usernameTaken: This username is taken. Choose another.
setup.codeGone: The setup code is no longer valid. Enter the current one from the console again.
setup.nameNotSaved: Your account is made, but the server name could not be saved. Change it later in Settings.
setup.cloudText: Linked, {{server}} takes invites by email, and people join and sign in here with their Orchester account. The cloud only vouches for who people are; it never sees your projects.
setup.cloudHint: Your browser goes to {{host}}, where you sign in and confirm. It brings back the cloud's keys, and {{server}} pins them. The server itself needs no internet for this.
setup.notNowHint: {{server}} works without it: people join with invite codes, and you link it later in Settings.
setup.noCloudText: This admin has no address for Orchester Cloud (ORCHESTER_ADMIN_CLOUD_URL), so it can't link from here. {{server}} works without it: people join with invite codes, and you link it later in Settings.
setup.notLinkedText: People join with invite codes, and admins sign in here with codes. Link it any time in Settings, from a browser that reaches the internet.
setup.next1Text: Name it and choose its slug: its address will be {{host}}/<slug>.
setup.next2Text: Sign in to Orchester Cloud in Orchester (Settings › Orchester) and {{server}} is offered. Without the internet: print an account code for yourself on the server (orchester-server account-code <username>), then Connect a server with it.
setup.next3Text: From each project's Invites, by email or with a code; people with no project yet from People.

cert.title: First visit: is this your server?
cert.body: {{server}} made its own certificate, so your browser warned before it showed this page. A page can't prove itself: one in between could show these same lines. Open the certificate from the address bar and compare its SHA-256 fingerprint with what the server's console prints (orchester-server tls show); trust it in the browser only if they match.
cert.footnote: Teams with their own certificate authority, or a public domain behind Caddy, never see this. Plain HTTP works only on the server itself (127.0.0.1).

link.conflict: Orchester Cloud refused: this server is linked to another Orchester account.
link.invalid: Orchester Cloud refused the link request: it was not valid or older than 10 minutes. Start again.
link.forbidden: Only admins link the server to Orchester Cloud.
link.refused: Linking did not finish: the server did not accept what Orchester Cloud sent. Start again.
link.unavailable: Linking did not finish: the server is not answering. Try again in a minute.
link.trip: That trip to Orchester Cloud took too long or came back to another browser. Start again.
link.expired: This form has expired. Reload the page and try again.

trip.title: Going to Orchester Cloud
trip.text: Your browser goes to Orchester Cloud to confirm it's you, then comes back here.
